resources.string: One clipboard for this phone and your computers.
It made its own secret key, which never leaves it and lets your devices recognise this phone. Now connect a device: tap Connect a new device and scan the QR code it shows.
On a computer, run cbb pair and scan the code it shows.
I already use Clipboard Bridge on another phone
On your other phone, tap + and scan this code. Keep this screen open.
QR code to join the group
Nothing new to send or fetch.

It can then add and remove devices with cbb pair and cbb revoke. Its keys sit in a file on the computer: whoever copies that file can act as an admin until another admin removes it. Do this only for a computer you keep safe.
It can then add and remove devices with cbb pair and cbb revoke. Its keys are in its hardware, which never lets them out.
It is an admin now: it adds and removes devices with cbb pair and cbb revoke.
Another admin froze this computer, as one does with a stolen one: it changes nothing and the others refuse it. Unfreeze it only if it is in safe hands; otherwise remove it.
It will no longer sync with your devices. To add it again, scan its QR code again.
It made the group. This phone takes the group over with a new key, and the other devices follow it.
Removed. The other devices refuse it from now on.
Only an admin phone can add or remove devices.
Lost a phone? Make a second phone an admin: on it, tap I already use Clipboard Bridge on another phone, then scan its code here with +.
Point the camera at the QR code of cbb pair, or at the one your other phone shows.
Paste the text of the QR code of cbb pair.
The camera is not allowed. Allow it in the app\'s settings to scan, or paste the text of the QR code of cbb pair.
Not a Clipboard Bridge QR code.
Add a computer to your group
Remove a device from your group
Take the group over from the lost phone
The computer joined but did not confirm it. Check cbb status on it.
Connect this phone to your home Wi-Fi, then try again.
No phone scanned the code in five minutes. Try again.
Too many wrong codes. Try again with a new code.
Could not read the clipboard, so it was left as it is. Copy the text again, then try again.
Only an admin phone can do this.
This computer keeps its keys in a file. Make it an admin first on its page, which warns what that means.
Could not reach the computer. Is it on the same network as this phone, and does its firewall let Clipboard Bridge in?
The code did not match. Run cbb pair on the computer again and scan the new code.
The computer refused. Run cbb pair on it again.
The other phone\'s group could not be joined. Try again.
Set a screen lock on this phone first: the group\'s keys need it.
The fingerprint, face or screen lock was not confirmed, so nothing changed.
What they copy comes to this phone. Send sends what this phone copied.
Send this text to your computers?
%1$s handed Clipboard Bridge a text of %2$d characters. It goes to every computer of the group.
Sync the clipboard with your computers?
%1$s opened Clipboard Bridge. Syncing may put your computers\' latest copy on this phone\'s clipboard, where that app could read it.
Share, the selection menu and the cbb send entry let any app hand Clipboard Bridge a text or start a sync, so the phone asks first. "Always for this app" lets that one app go without asking.
None: the phone asks every app.

Notices when you copy text, then reads the clipboard for a moment and sends the text to your computers. With remote paste on, it puts an admin\'s text into the text field that has the focus. It reads nothing else on the screen.

Android lets an app read the clipboard only while it is in front. Turn Clipboard Bridge on in Accessibility, and what you copy goes to your computers without a tap; Android then says \"CBB pasted from your clipboard\" each time. Without it, use the Send clipboard tile, the notification\'s Send button, or Share.
If Android says the setting is restricted: open App info, tap ⋮, choose Allow restricted settings, then try again.
This phone is the group\'s hub

While the app is open, this phone is the hub of a group without a computer: the other phones, TVs and lite members on the home network connect to it, and with a forwarder they reach it from afar too. The forwarder only passes encrypted packets; it learns the group\'s tag, this phone\'s tunnel key and the addresses, never what is copied. A computer that is always on is the better hub; until then this phone does it.
Off: this phone is no hub.
Waiting for the app: the hub works while the app is open.
The hub at home only: add a forwarder for sync away from home.
Registered with the forwarder: devices away from home reach this phone.
The forwarder does not take this phone. Check its address and key.
On a home network: devices here connect to this phone.
This network is not one of the hub\'s home networks: devices here do not see this phone.
Give the forwarder\'s address with its port and its key, as cbb forward prints them, or leave both empty.
Keep the hub running in the background (uses the battery)
This phone is the hub: sync works while the app is open.
This phone is the hub, in the background too.

When the phone is not on the home network, it syncs through the WireGuard tunnel of your own hub, a computer of the group set up with cbb global hub; its port is reachable from the internet, but only through WireGuard with the group\'s keys. The hub answers this phone the next time it connects at home. Nothing goes anywhere else, and without the tunnel there is no connection. Turning it off forgets this phone\'s tunnel key.
Waiting for the hub: open the app at home once, near a computer of the group.
Connecting to the hub through the tunnel…
Connected to the hub through the tunnel.
The hub does not answer through the tunnel.
Error messages show the error underneath them, to find out what failed. Tap the version seven times to see this switch.
Every device of the group shows the new name.
Renamed. The other devices show the new name as soon as they hear of it.
One tap sends what this phone copied to your computers.
Its copies stay on it and the group\'s do not come; sending or fetching by hand still works.
Its copies go to the group, and the group\'s come to it.
The group\'s copies come to it; its own stay on it.
Its copies go to the group; the group\'s do not come.
The computer did not answer. It may be offline, or run an older version of Clipboard Bridge.
The app notifies of these as soon as it hears of them; the service hears of them in the background too. A paired watch shows them as well.
A device joined or was removed
A device was frozen or unfrozen
The hub does not answer away from home
%1$s was frozen: the others refuse it until an admin unfreezes it.
%1$s took the group over: it holds the group\'s root now.
For a device that is not on your network, such as a parent\'s computer: share the invitation file with its owner, who joins with cbb pair -invite. It works once, for an hour, while this app is open.
The invitation is open until %1$s. Share its file only with the person who joins: anyone who has it can ask to join.
A device (%1$s) used the invitation. Admit it only if the device shows the same fingerprint:
The device joined the group; it appears in the list once it connects.
The invitation expired without being used.
The invitation closed after three failed attempts. Make a new one.
An invitation needs the hub registered with its forwarder. Check the forwarder above.
Move the hub to a computer
Move the hub to a computer
A computer that is always on keeps sync away from home working while this app is closed. The devices that reach this phone from afar move with it.
%1$s is always on. Make it the hub, so that sync away from home works while this app is closed?
The devices that reach this phone from afar move to %1$s, and this phone becomes its client. Sync away from home must be on there (cbb global on).
The computer is the hub now; this phone reaches it from afar.
The computer did not become the hub.
The hub can move only while it runs with a forwarder.
Off: this phone meets nobody at a relay.
Waiting: the relay works while the app syncs.
At the relay: no other device of the group is there now.
At the relay; devices of the group there: %1$d.
The relay does not take this phone. Check its address and key.
Give the relay\'s address with its port and its key, as cbb relay prints them, or leave both empty.

For a group without a hub of its own: the devices meet at a relay, such as one set up with cbb relay, while the app syncs. The clipboard stays encrypted between the devices, but the relay learns which of them are online and their addresses, and which talk to each other, when and how much. Leave both fields empty to stop.

The clipboard stays encrypted end to end between the devices: the relay cannot read it or pose as a device. It does learn, while the devices use it, which devices of the group are online and their internet addresses, and which of them talk to each other, when and how much they send. A hub of the group\'s own lets none of this out. Use a relay you run yourself, or one whose operator you trust with this.
It goes where %1$s\'s keyboard focus is, once its user turned remote paste on there.

A paste suits most apps; typing suits those that take no paste, and only up to 4 KB. Enter runs a command in a terminal, so the computer takes it only when its user allowed that. A secret leaves no trace in the computer\'s log or clipboard.
%1$s has no quick action turned on. Its user turns them on there, with sudo cbb action enable.
The computer defines what each action does, and runs it only for the admins its user allowed.
It happens a minute from now; until then, Cancel the reboot or shutdown stops it.
The device did not run the action.
Turn off the quick actions on %1$s?
No admin can run them there until its user turns them on again on the device itself.
The quick actions are off there.
Let the group\'s admins paste here

An admin of the group then puts a text into the text field that has the focus on this phone, from its own app or with cbb paste. This phone shows who pasted, and keeps a log of the last pastes without their text. Never on the lock screen.
It pastes through the service "Send my copies by themselves", which is off: turn it on in the system\'s accessibility settings.
